about: How fast each motor follows its command (spec: Copter analyzers, heavy-lift, 'Actuator response'; engine/src/flight_insights/analyzers/motor_lag.py). The command is rebuilt from the mixer's inputs logged every loop in RATE and the frame's mixer factors; the answer is the ESC's RPM. Uncalibrated: the thresholds for a slow motor are the app's starting points until real heavy-lift flights have been compared.
sources: ArduCopter/Copter.cpp at Copter-4.7.0: with LOG_BITMASK bit 0 (fast attitude) RATE is logged every loop, its ROut, POut, YOut and AOut being the mixer's roll, pitch, yaw and throttle inputs (AC_AttitudeControl_Logging.cpp Write_Rate: motors get_roll() + get_roll_ff() and so on); RCOU is logged at 10 Hz (ten_hz_logging_loop)
libraries/AP_ESC_Telem/AP_ESC_Telem.cpp at Copter-4.7.0: ESC rows are written by a 100 Hz task (AP_Vehicle.cpp scheduler) whenever an ESC's RPM or telemetry is new, timestamped when written

knowledge/frames/<version>.json, read from AP_MotorsMatrix.cpp and checked against SITL (knowledge/tools/check_motor_frames_sitl.py): each motor's command is its throttle, roll, pitch and yaw factors times the mixer's inputs while no motor is at a limit

copter/source/docs/autotune.rst (ArduPilot wiki): AutoTune can request very large and fast changes in output, which can cause ESC sync issues with low-KV motors (under 500 KV): large props and low-KV motors respond slowly
